international.title: Asia-Pacific markets rally as Huang’s return to Nvidia reignites AI trade, despite US political backlash – business live
international.summary: Rolling coverage of the latest economic and financial news Republican senators criticize Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang The surge in stock markets since Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia was announced shows that investors are “willing to re-engage with the AI theme when uncertainty recedes”, says Christian Stocker , lead equity strategist for UniCredit Munich . But… Stocker argues that the rally reflected relief that the AI supply chain and investment cycle are unlikely to be abruptly disrupted, rather than renewed conviction that all concerns have disappeared. Questions about financing structures, profitability and the ultimate returns on AI spending remain largely unresolved. In other words, the debate has shifted. Investors are no longer asking whether AI investment will continue. They are increasingly asking whether the path from investment to monetisation will be slower, more uneven and more dependent on favourable financing conditions than previously assumed. Recent market volatility suggests that the AI narrative remains intact, but the market is becoming less willing to assume a straight-line path to future earnings growth. With fears of an AI slowdown receding, it also led markets to price back in a more hawkish path for the Federal Reserve over the months ahead. So for the next meeting in December, markets are once again fully pricing in a 25bp hike, with 26.1bps priced in for that decision (+3.1bps on the day) .
